chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What is sufficient of recitation in the last two rak'at?' He said: 'That you say: Subhan Allah, and al-Hamd lillah, and la ilaha illa Allah, and Allah Akbar, and you say Takbir and bow.'

key_terms.وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ: and all praise is due to God
key_terms.وَتُكَبِّرَ: and you say Takbir (God is Greater)
key_terms.وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: and there is no god but God

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum recitation required in the last two rak'at of prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies the minimal recitation (Qira'ah) for the last two rak'at, emphasizing that the four phrases of glorification and affirmation, coupled with the physical act of bowing, suffice for validity. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the obligatory recitation in the first two rak'at and the more flexible, often shorter recitation in the subsequent ones, reflecting the practical ease granted to the worshipper. The emphasis on 'Subhan Allah' and 'La ilaha illa Allah' underscores the theological core of prayer as an act of divine transcendence and monotheistic affirmation.
